How is Utah organized when you sell a house here?

Utah has 29 counties, and almost every step of a house sale touches one of them. The county assessor values the property, the treasurer collects the tax bill, and the recorder files the deed and any liens. City hall matters for permits and code questions, but the county offices hold the paper that decides whether a sale can close.

Most sellers deal with one of four counties first. Salt Lake County is the largest by a wide margin, and Utah, Davis and Weber counties follow it along the Wasatch Front. Farther south, Washington County covers St. George and Hurricane, and Iron County covers Cedar City. Our county pages cover the offices and tax steps in more detail for Salt Lake County, Washington County, Tooele County and Wasatch County.

What are the main Utah rules a seller should know at a glance?

TopicWhat Utah law says
Property tax due dateNovember 30 each year, or the next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday (Utah Code 59-2-1331)
Late penalty2.5 percent or $10, whichever is greater, falling to 1 percent if paid by January 31 (59-2-1331)
Residential exemption45 percent off the value of a primary residence, up to one acre per unit (59-2-103)
Value appeal deadlineThe later of September 15 or 45 days after the valuation notice (59-2-1004)
Trust deed foreclosureAt least three months between the notice of default and the notice of sale (57-1-24)
Small estate affidavit30 days after death, estate value under $100,000 (75-3-1201)
Homestead exemption$42,000 for a primary residence as set in 2019, adjusted yearly (78B-5-503)
Tax saleHeld by the county auditor in May or June (59-2-1351)

How do Utah property taxes affect a sale?

Taxes follow the parcel, so unpaid ones show up at closing. Utah bills are due November 30, and a payment that is postmarked after that date is delinquent. The penalty starts at 2.5 percent of the delinquent amount or $10, whichever is greater. It drops to 1 percent when everything is paid by the next January 31, and interest runs after that.

Utah also gives a break to homeowners. A primary residence receives a 45 percent reduction in its taxable value, and the exemption covers no more than one acre per residential unit.

If you think the county valued your house too high, you can apply to the county board of equalization. The deadline is the later of September 15 or 45 days after the county auditor sends the valuation notice. The board has 60 days to decide after you apply. Our Utah property tax guide walks through the process in plain steps.

When taxes stay unpaid long enough, the county auditor holds a tax sale in May or June, either at the courthouse door or electronically. Notice goes to the last known recorded owner, to the occupant of an improved property and to other interests of record. You will find the redemption details on our Utah tax sale page, and the treasurer can give you a payoff figure for your parcel.

How does foreclosure work in Utah?

Most Utah home loans use a trust deed, and that allows a sale without going to court. The trustee records a notice of default with the county recorder. At least three months must pass before the trustee can move forward with a sale.

After that window, the notice of sale has to be published in a newspaper at least three times over three consecutive weeks, and the last publication has to fall between 10 and 30 days before the sale. The trustee also posts the notice on the property and at the recorder's office at least 20 days before the sale. The auction takes place between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. at a courthouse serving the county.

You have more room than many owners realize in that first three months. The owner, or anyone with a lien that ranks behind the trust deed, can pay the full amount due plus the lender's actual costs and fees and bring the loan current. The trustee must then cancel the recorded notice of default.

People facing a default usually have three options:

  • Cure the default by paying the arrears, fees and costs inside the three month window.
  • Sell the house before the auction date and pay off the lender from the proceeds.
  • Talk to the lender about a modification or other workout.

Ask the trustee named in your notice for a payoff statement before you decide.

What should heirs know about selling an inherited house in Utah?

Start with the title, not the price. Utah's small estate affidavit lets a successor collect certain property 30 days after a death when the entire estate, after liens, does not exceed $100,000 and no one has applied to be personal representative. The statute is written for tangible personal property, debts and securities, so do not assume it moves a house into your name.

A few facts shape the timeline for real estate:

  • A buyer and a title company will want proof that the person signing the deed has legal authority.
  • A mortgage on the home stays in place and keeps accruing until it is paid.
  • Property tax bills keep arriving on November 30 whether or not the estate is open.

Our Utah probate guide and estate and inheritance tax page cover the next steps. For a decision about your own case, the district court clerk or a probate attorney is the right call.

Does the Utah homestead exemption matter to a seller?

It can. Utah law protects part of the value of a primary residence from judgment creditors. When the statute was last rewritten in 2019, the figure was $42,000 for a primary residence, with a household cap of $84,000 for jointly owned property, and the State Auditor adjusts the amounts each year using the Consumer Price Index. Check the auditor's current figures before you rely on a number.

The protection has limits. Liens for property taxes, for the purchase price and for child support, along with consensual liens such as a mortgage, are not blocked. After a sale, proceeds up to the exemption amount stay protected from levy for one year after you receive them. Our homestead exemption page explains how owners claim it.

What if the house has tenants in it?

A tenant's rights do not disappear because the owner wants to sell. Utah's unlawful detainer statute sets different notice periods depending on the lease and the problem:

  • A month to month tenant must receive a notice to leave at least 15 calendar days before the end of the rental period.
  • A tenant at will can be asked to leave on at least five calendar days of notice.
  • An unpaid rent notice gives the tenant three business days to pay or leave.
  • Other lease violations carry a three calendar day notice.

If a lender is foreclosing on a rental, the statute requires a notice to tenants that mentions a federal right to stay until the lease ends or 90 days after a notice to vacate, whichever is later. Read more on our eviction process page and landlord and tenant page.

What does an as-is cash sale look like in Utah?

An as-is sale means the buyer takes the house in its current condition, so you do not paint, patch or replace anything first. The paperwork is still the same kind of paperwork: a purchase contract, a title search, payoff letters for any lien and a recorded deed at the county recorder.

Radon is one Utah item worth knowing about before you list or sell. The state environmental quality agency says about one in three Utah homes has elevated radon, and the EPA action level is 4 picocuries per liter. The agency puts a typical fix at around $1,500, and it points owners to certified mitigators. Test results can come up in a buyer's inspection, so run a test early if you can.

Taxes on the gain are a separate question, covered on our capital gains page.

Who should you call with a question about your property?

Utah keeps the answers at the county level, so start there:

  • County assessor, for your valuation and the residential exemption.
  • County treasurer, for a tax payoff and delinquency status.
  • County recorder, for liens, deeds and any recorded notice of default.
  • County auditor, for the tax sale schedule.

Ask the office directly for anything your situation depends on. Our guides by city and county point you to the pages for your area.

Frequently asked questions

How many counties does Utah have?

Utah has 29 counties. Salt Lake, Utah, Davis and Weber counties are the four largest by population.

When are Utah property taxes due?

November 30 each year, or the next business day when that date falls on a weekend or holiday. Late payments carry a penalty of 2.5 percent or $10, whichever is greater.

How long does a Utah foreclosure take?

Under a trust deed, at least three months must pass after the notice of default is recorded before the trustee can give notice of sale. The sale notice then runs for several more weeks.

Can I stop a foreclosure in Utah?

Within three months of the recorded notice of default, you can pay the amount due plus the lender's costs and fees and reinstate the loan.

Do I need probate to sell an inherited Utah house?

Not always, but the small estate affidavit is written for personal property. Ask a probate attorney or the district court clerk about the deed for your case.

What is the Utah residential property tax exemption?

A primary residence receives a 45 percent reduction in taxable value, for up to one acre per residential unit.

Can I sell a house with tenants in Utah?

Yes. Existing lease rights and the notice periods in Utah's unlawful detainer statute still apply to the new owner's plans.

Does a cash buyer need repairs done first?

No. An as-is sale means you leave the house in its current condition and the buyer decides what work to do.
